cs.t: I had one of these with an extra battery  https://www.bestbuy.com/site/apc-back-ups-pro-1000va-battery...  back in the day I had slow ADSL (2 Mbit/sec) from the phone company central office so my DSL would stay up when the power went out.  That system could keep my DSL modem and cordless phone up and running for about two days or so,  so with laptops and tablets I'd have 21st century comms for a weekend when the power goes out. They upgraded my DSL to ADSL2 served from a fiber node a mile or so from my house,  now I get highly reliable and consistent 20 Mbit/sec,  except when the power goes out in which case the node goes down.  I donated the UPS to my local reuse center because there wasn't much point in it. I have a small tower computer I use as a server and thought about plugging it into the UPS but decided it wasn't worth the trouble because the runtime wouldn't be good.  It would probably be better than 5 minutes,  but it's not "run through a power outage",  it is,  "have a short period of terror in which to save your documents".  Keeping the DSL up was "life-changing" though because it meant I could still keep in touch with the people at work.
cs.th: Ask HN: Make sure a desktop computer doesn't shutdown because of power outage
